messages:
Alex: FYI paging eng-runtime — customer acme-prod seeing a big spike in 504s from hosted API in us-west-2 starting ~11:02 PT. Pattern looks like request queue tail timeouts, not auth. sample request_ids: r-7c9a1f, r-4b3d2a
Sam: Single tenant or multi-tenant?
Alex: Single tenant. They ramped from 30rps -> ~250rps with many short requests (~50-200 tokens). Continuous batching backlog grew.
Maria: Gateway logs show repeated queue depth hits and handler timeouts. Quick excerpt:
```
[11:02:12] gateway: enqueue id=r-7c9a1f depth=512
[11:02:12] batcher: backlog_len=128 active_batches=6 kv_cache_miss=0
[11:02:13] router: dispatch_delay_ms=2300
[11:02:14] handler: handler_timeout_ms=5000 -> 504
```
Sam: @Ops-bot can we bump ingress.queue.max_depth for the hosted pool in us-west-2 as an emergency mitigation?
Ops-bot: @here initiating emergency config change: `ingress.queue.max_depth=1024` on pool us-west-2. Rolling to 3/3 nodes, will take ~90s per node. Note: this increases memory pressure and may increase tail latency.
Support-bot: Escalation created ESCL-5463, customer notified, ETA for engineering triage 30m.
Jonah: Short-term mitigation ideas: 1) increase queue depth (done), 2) enable per-tenant burst isolation, 3) apply aggressive prefix/KV caching for their workload.
Maria: Repro steps for local triage:
1) `git checkout replay-traces && cargo run --bin replay -- --trace acme-prod --rate 250`
2) `stress-batcher --concurrency 16 --seq-len 64 --model gpt-medium`
3) watch gateway metrics: `promql: gateway_queue_depth{pool=\"us-west-2\"}`
Expected: enqueue stalls, dispatch_delay spikes, tail 504s.
Sam: Confirmed, after bump tail 504s dropped from ~12% -> ~1.8% within 6 minutes. Still seeing higher p95 latency (~600ms -> 1.1s).
Maria: Root-cause hypothesis: continuous-batcher scheduling degenerates under highly lopsided short-request workloads, causing long per-request waiting in queue (queue-shear) and missed batch formation deadlines. Also observed uneven worker allocation (thinpool starvation).
Alex: Customer-facing note drafted and sent: apologized, explained transient congestion and mitigation. Offering follow-up with perf report and options (dedicated burst pool or rate-limit throttles).
Jonah: Action items:
- eng-runtime: triage scheduling algorithm and thinpool balancing (owner: Maria)
- ops: evaluate adding per-tenant burst pools and alerting on queue_depth > 75% for 2m (owner: Sam)
- support: coordinate customer follow-up + credits if SLA breached (owner: Support-bot)
Maria: Triage checklist posted to runbook PR #3827. Please attach p95 traces, batcher histograms, kernel/steal cpu metrics, and the replay trace to the ticket.
Sam: Uploading traces to /shared/esc/6776543210 and enabling temporary prefix caching for the tenant. :thumbsup:
Alex: Will follow up later with postmortem once triage complete. Thanks all.
